items.q: In a program the integer 213 is divided by 25 using integer division. What remainder is produced?
items.s: 213 = 8 x 25 + 13, so the remainder is 13.

items.q: A linear search is used on an array of 874 records and the wanted record is the last one. How many records must be examined?

items.s: Repeated division stops when the remainder is zero, which takes 7 steps here.

items.q: A nested loop has an outer loop that runs 9 times and an inner loop that runs 21 times for every pass of the outer loop. How many times does the innermost statement execute?
items.s: Innermost executions = outer passes x inner passes = 9 x 21 = 189.

items.q: A loop accumulates the first 6 terms of the series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... starting from 1. What total does it reach?

items.q: A recursive routine computes the Fibonacci number F(12), where F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1. What value is returned?
items.s: Following F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) up to n = 12 gives 144.

items.q: A naive recursive routine for F(13) is entered once, where F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1 and each call makes two more. Including the first entry, how many calls are made in all?
items.s: Naive recursion makes 2 x F(14) - 1 = 753 calls in total.

items.q: A routine raises 2 to the power 4 by repeated multiplication in a loop. What is the result?

items.s: 5090 falls to 1 after 13 rounds of rounding up to the next integer.

items.q: A loop sums the decimal digits of the integer 213369. What is the final value of the total?
items.s: The digits of 213369 add up to 24.

items.q: How many bits are set to one in the binary representation of the integer 235?

items.s: The largest value needs 16 bits because 2^15 is below 52762 and 2^16 is not.

items.q: A matrix with 6 rows and 9 columns is multiplied into a matrix with 9 rows and 9 columns. How many scalar multiplications does a straightforward routine perform?

items.q: A bubble sort is applied to an array of 36 items and it always runs the full set of passes. How many comparisons of adjacent pairs does it make?
items.s: Comparisons = N(N-1)/2 = 36 x 35 / 2 = 630.

items.q: A bubble sort is applied to an array of 18 items that is in the worst possible order. What is the number of passes needed to be certain that the array is ordered?
items.s: Each pass settles one item, so at most N - 1 = 17 passes are needed.

items.q: A selection sort is applied to an array of 16 items. What is the number of exchanges it performs?
items.s: One exchange is made for each position except the last, so N - 1 = 15.

items.q: A binary search halves the search range at every step. Starting with an array of 1218 elements, how many halvings are needed to reduce the range to a single element?
items.s: 1218 reduced by repeated halving reaches 1 after 10 halvings.

items.q: The bisection method starts from an interval of width 8 and must reach an accuracy of 0.002. What is the least number of halvings required?
items.s: After k halvings the width is 8/2^k, so 2^k must reach 8/0.002 = 4000, giving k = 12.

The trapezoidal rule with 5 equal intervals is applied to f(x) = x^2 over the range 0 to 2. What value does it give?
items.s: Strip width h = 2/5 = 0.4; adding the strip areas gives 2.72.
